text: What is the use of a book without pictures or conversations?
Hush, Alice dear.
I wonder how many miles I've fallen by this time?
Dinah'll miss me very much to-night, I should think!
Do cats eat bats? Do cats eat bats?… Do bats eat cats?
Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!
Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting!
That certainly was not here before.
No, I'll look first, and see whether it's marked 'poison' or not.
What a curious feeling! I must be shutting up like a telescope.
For it might end, you know, in my going out altogether, like a candle.
Come, there's no use in crying like that! I advise you to leave off this minute!
Well, I'll eat it. And if it makes me grow larger, I can reach the key;
and if it makes me grow smaller, I can creep under the door.
So either way I'll get into the garden, and I don't care which happens!
Which way? Which way?
Curiouser and curiouser!
Now I'm opening out like the largest telescope that ever was! Good-bye, feet!
You ought to be ashamed of yourself, a great girl like you, to go on crying in this way!
Stop this moment, I tell you!
Oh! the Duchess, the Duchess! Oh! won't she be savage if I've kept her waiting!
If you please, sir—
Dear, dear! How queer everything is to-day! And yesterday things went on just as usual.
I wonder if I've been changed in the night? But if I'm not the same, who in the world am I?
Ah, that's the great puzzle!
Let me see: four times five is twelve, and four times six is thirteen… London is the capital of Paris—
No, that's all wrong, I'm certain! I must have been changed for Mabel!
Oh dear, I do wish they would put their heads down! I am so very tired of being all alone here!
That was a narrow escape!
And now for the garden!
I must have fallen into the sea! And in that case I can go back by railway.
I wish I hadn't cried so much!
I shall be punished for it now, I suppose, by being drowned in my own tears!
That will be a queer thing, to be sure! However, everything is queer to-day.
